extracted.intended_audience: reporters, journalists, and nominators for the George Polk Awards
extracted.subtask_description: Award nomination and selection criteria used by the George Polk Awards to recognize individual reporters for distinguished journalism, emphasizing investigative, courageous, original, and influential work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Intrepid, bold, and influential work
rubrics_metrics.description: Awards focus on 'intrepid, bold, and influential work of reporters.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Polk Awards place a premium on reporting that demonstrates boldness and influence; selection emphasizes work that is both daring and has measurable effect or resonance. Factors listed below (investigative work, resourcefulness, courage, originality, impact) are examples of what constitutes 'intrepid, bold, and influential' work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Investigative work
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Preference for reporting that uncovers new information or perspectives through sustained inquiry; work should be original in conception or findings, display resourceful reporting techniques, and provoke public consideration or debate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Resourcefulness
rubrics_metrics.description: Resourcefulness — pursuit of stories despite difficulty.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Judges value reporters who pursue important stories even when access is limited or obstacles exist (legal, logistical, institutional). Resourcefulness can include creative sourcing, data work, persistent field reporting, or overcoming censorship/obstruction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Courage in journalism
rubrics_metrics.description: Courage in journalism — willingness to face danger or pushback.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognition is given to reporters who accept personal risk, legal threats, or significant pushback in order to report important stories. Courage may be physical, legal, professional, or political in nature.

rubrics_metrics.name: Originality
rubrics_metrics.description: Originality — first to surface a story.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Awarded work often brings new facts or angles to light, being the first to report or frame an issue in a consequential way. Originality includes novel sourcing, unique storytelling approaches, or breaking previously hidden information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Impact / influence
rubrics_metrics.description: Impact / influence — visible effect on policy or public discourse.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Selection favors reporting that produces demonstrable change such as policy reforms, official investigations, resignations, public debate shifts, or other measurable consequences in public life.

rubrics_metrics.name: Award categories
rubrics_metrics.description: Awards are given across multiple categories.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Listed categories include Foreign Reporting; National Reporting; Local Reporting; Business Reporting; Environmental Reporting; Photojournalism; Science Reporting; Political Reporting; International Reporting; Podcast / Audio Reporting. Entries are evaluated within these topical/format categories.

rubrics_metrics.name: Holding power accountable
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Works that scrutinize institutions, officials, corporations, or other centers of power and illuminate misconduct, negligence, or abuse are especially valued.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exposing wrongdoing or hidden truth
rubrics_metrics.description: Implicit criterion: exposing wrongdoing or hidden truth.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reports that reveal corruption, fraud, abuse, or previously concealed facts—thereby informing the public—align with the award's mission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinctive reporter voice / individual achievement
rubrics_metrics.description: Implicit criterion: distinctive reporter voice and individual achievement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Polk Awards honor individual reporters rather than organizations; judges look for clear individual contribution, distinctive reporting voice or perspective, and personal accountability for the work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Persistence through obstacles
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sustained effort in the face of barriers—such as long-term investigation, repeated attempts to access information, or enduring legal/organizational resistance—is a positive factor.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stories that produce change
rubrics_metrics.description: Implicit criterion: stories that produce change.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Beyond exposure, the most favored work is that which leads to tangible outcomes: reforms, policy changes, institutional responses, or concrete shifts in public understanding or behavior.
